A five year old's head would be spinning even if you tried to summarize the events of this long-drawn out battle where neither side can agree what they are fighting over. Also, I am bad at describing things, but I want to anyways.

It's ugly, but it may boil down to the following. GamerGate (GG) was the scandal that involved a conflict of interest created by a sexual relationship between a developer and a video game journalist. It has evolved into various camps and possibly two sides that can each be said to have a legitimate critique of the video game industry.

If you are a GamerGater, you are pro-GG. Their stereotype is the avid gamer that is male and connected to the online video gaming community. Anti-GG supporters are harder to describe. Anti-GGs are possibly allied with feminists, SJWs, and certain industry insiders. This side also includes people, such as journalists and online personalities, that were the target of the original accusations and subsequent attacks. You probably know about some of the stereotypes, especially those associated with SJWs, but they may simply be described as a new wave of female voices that have rose to prominence in the video game industry.

There's no simple way to describe the true intent nor pure goals of either side. You might try to compromise and say that any wrongdoing that either side has evidence for can be eventually corrected, but there is simply too much distrust. Trying to address these issues would stir up renewed controversy and everyone would end up hating you. You can attempt to describe a perfect world, but it will be a long, treacherous road to get there.

Video game journalists and developers alike should be able to operate free from influence and political pressure. Political correctness is actually a tool and may be leveraged by a vocal minority. This political game can become dangerous because zealots from either side will resort to trying to ruin people's lives in order to either prevent any opposing voices from being disruptive or get revenge for losses they suffered. This is where most of the controversy stems from. However, if you get beyond this, you may actually see that females may not have been treated entirely fairly despite successes they may have seen in the video game industry. Whether they are newcomers or veterans, they are allowed to try to change the way video games are made for the better as long as it does not destroy the creativity or free expression of their contemporaries.

To go more deeply, there's a lot of misinformation out there as well as questionable incidents and personal attacks from both sides. You can compare it to bipartisan politics where each side constantly attacks and blames the other for unethical behavior even when it is an inherent problem of the system that they are both guilty of condoning. The problem is that each side has been corrupted, and you have lots of shady characters on each side that "ruin the message". The biggest two messages from each side are probably the following. GamerGaters say that they were originally trying to expose unethical relationships in video game journalism (reviewing), and they say that the quality of games is suffering in various ways due to political correctness. Anti-GGs say that this is really about pushback against a new wave of female influence within the video game industry, and they say that female figures are attacked at every turn simply for wanting progress however it is defined.

My personal view is probably reflected in my words despite my attempts to be fair. I feel that female video game insiders have support systems and will be accommodated in various ways by the industry. Twitter, Tumblr, and other social media will always be a insane mess that muddies the waters. GamerGate and similar scandals needed to be addressed, but the guilty probably have too many allies that are practiced at throwing down smoke screens and playing the victim. Extremists exist on both sides so you have attacks, counterattacks, and even people attacking themselves in order to accomplish their political goals. Since the truth may never be clear, it would probably be best if people forgot about GamerGate since it's no longer worth the damage being done to the industry. Yet, certain people won't be willing to give up because it gives the other side too much power.

To add on others, the reason it's fizzled out a bit is twofold.

  1. Countless in-fighting about whether it should be about ethics or fighting marxism/e-celebs acting like they are leaders of what's supposed to be an anon group

  2. People did some digging and ended up finding that government funded organizations specializing in social media are involved and noped the fuck out

I think the simplest explanation is that there was a secret Google Docs group called GameJournoPros that was made up of an overwhelming majority of games journalists. In this group, they conspired behind closed doors to plug specific games (generally games they had some kind of personal financial stake in) and to pan games that didn't agree with their personal beliefs.

A member of this group Ed Snowden'ed on the rest of them. Instead of just admitting what they were doing, the group pushes an industry-wide group of articles attempting to basically erase the 'gamer' identity. The gist of these articles was "everyone plays video games now, gamers don't exist, the only people resisting are sexist men who want video games to remain a boys club".

This lead to #notyourshield, a movement of female/black/gay/etc gamers who were very vocal about the fact that they consider themselves gamers, and that the supposed sexism and racism of gaming culture were lies.

In typical SJW fashion, the GameJournoPros accuse all of the members of #notyourshield of being sockpuppet accounts made by white males in order to discredit their articles. They claim relentless harassment from gamers, but are unable to provide any evidence of said harassment that isn't later proven to be farcical.

Feeling betrayed, gamers begin a mailing campaign to the sponsors of the GameJourno-associated websites (Gawker, Kotaku, Vice, Polygon... pretty much all the major news sites that publish gaming articles) to get them to pull sponsorship. A bunch of them do.

And ever since then, there's been extreme animosity between gaming journalists and their supposed audience.
